scenario: An OpenAI cost backfill groups user and project successfully for recent dates but returns 400 for an older range.
mechanism: Supported grouping depends on organization and historical period; generic retry or empty fallback can manufacture zero historical spend.
detection: Persist HTTP result and query hash; probe capability by range without converting rejected dimensions to no-data.
response: Retry an explicitly supported coarser query under a separate extraction receipt; retain unavailable attribution and expose scope difference.
test_assertion: Rejected detailed history does not create zero rows; coarser monetary totals appear once with attribution unavailable; detail and aggregate are never added.
residual_limit: Supported coarser data still cannot reconstruct historical human/team attribution.

scenario: Anthropic default-workspace Priority Tier usage appears with null workspace and no matching cost.
mechanism: Null denotes default workspace, while Priority Tier charges are excluded from the cost endpoint; treating either as missing/zero hides real exposure.
detection: Interpret null by provider field contract; inspect usage service_tier and cost coverage manifest.
response: Map an explicit provider-default workspace identity; record Priority Tier cost exclusion and retain its usage without invented charges.
test_assertion: Default workspace usage remains in company usage totals; all-in reported spend is incomplete until another authorized financial basis covers Priority Tier.
residual_limit: Contractual Priority pricing/commitment data is not obtained from this endpoint.

scenario: A CUR refresh replaces earlier files while a reader is ingesting; a retry also sees different classic-CUR line item IDs.
mechanism: Mixing delivery generations or treating report-local IDs as stable events duplicates or loses spend.
detection: Capture manifest/checksums and verify every required chunk belongs to one delivery; record report/partition namespace.
response: Stage one complete immutable generation and activate atomically; retry the complete generation on inconsistency; preserve earlier version.
test_assertion: Displayed total equals exactly one complete generation; interrupted import cannot partially change current totals; identical re-import has no monetary effect.
residual_limit: Later finalized-period credits still require deeper scheduled reconciliation.

scenario: Azure Actual and Amortized exports for the same period are both imported, followed by an invoice-level rounding adjustment without resource ID.
mechanism: Alternative accounting views are summed and unassigned rounding is dropped, creating a total that matches neither selected basis nor invoice.
detection: Record dataset financial basis and billing scope; compare complete-period controls; allow no-resource adjustments.
response: Keep view-specific totals; preserve adjustment as company-level unattributed charge and allocate only through an explicit separate policy.
test_assertion: Actual plus Amortized never contributes a combined total; invoice reconciliation includes signed rounding adjustment exactly once.
residual_limit: Allocated team shares of company adjustments remain policy choices, not provider facts.

scenario: A Google regional export is enabled today and returns no prior-month rows; another multi-region export is still processing its initial backfill.
mechanism: Region-dependent history and initial delivery lag are mistaken for genuine zero historical consumption.
detection: Record export enablement date, dataset location, backfill state and earliest verified covered date.
response: Mark unsupported/pending history separately; choose a shorter validated window or another authorized historical export.
test_assertion: No pre-enablement zero-filled series is produced; forecasting eligibility changes only after coverage evidence, not after an empty successful query.
residual_limit: Missing earlier data may be unrecoverable through that export.

scenario: Vertex workload migrates from PayGo to Provisioned Throughput while continuing to send team labels.
mechanism: Provisioned Throughput silently ignores request billing labels; apparent team spend falls even though company commitment spending continues.
detection: Monitor consumption-model mix and attributed-cost fraction; compare billing scope totals with team label totals.
response: Retain company cost; mark team allocation unresolved; apply separately authorized resource/commitment mapping rather than extrapolate vanished label totals.
test_assertion: Migration raises an attribution-coverage change, not a team savings conclusion; no team zero is inferred from absent labels.
residual_limit: Shared provisioned capacity allocation requires a company policy and additional evidence.

scenario: Cursor subscription-included activity has a nonzero cost valuation, and spend fields contain fractional cents.
mechanism: Adding overall spend valuation to subscription fees double counts inclusion; integer-cent parsing silently loses precision.
detection: Inspect isChargeable/kind and current-cycle spend bases; reconcile decimal totals with source controls.
response: Store included valuation separately from incremental charge; retain exact original decimal cents and contract basis.
test_assertion: Included usage never independently increases payable total; sub-cent amounts round only under explicit display/settlement rules, and import round-trip preserves original values.
residual_limit: Current-cycle endpoint alone does not supply complete historical seat invoices.

scenario: An employee with an enterprise-managed Copilot seat is queried through a personal billing endpoint as the enterprise switches from premium requests to AI credits.
mechanism: Wrong payer scope produces absent usage, while unchanged series names concatenate incompatible request and credit quantities.
detection: Resolve billed entity from seat/contract evidence; validate quantity unit and endpoint/version by effective date.
response: Read authorized organization/enterprise scope; split quantity bases and retain monetary basis/period metadata across migration.
test_assertion: Empty personal result never asserts enterprise zero; request and credit units cannot be summed; monetary comparisons require compatible currency/category coverage.
residual_limit: Historical contract transition and pools still need tenant-specific verification.

scenario: Claude Code users change from Console authentication to an Enterprise subscription or cloud-provider login midweek.
mechanism: Console Analytics ceases to cover those sessions; a model interprets the drop as lower activity, while underlying spend moves to another payer/feed.
detection: Track source product/authentication coverage and join approved account migration evidence; compare alternate billing scopes without assuming overlap.
response: Close the old coverage interval, introduce the new source with explicit overlap resolution, and retain activity/cost basis separately.
test_assertion: Migration yields a coverage/regime marker and does not manufacture user inactivity; overlapping analytics and provider charges are never additive.
residual_limit: No cross-provider event identifier is guaranteed; unresolved overlap can prevent exhaustive totals.

scenario: A ChatGPT workspace key has only the legacy Codex analytics scope and unified daily analytics access fails.
mechanism: Connector treats a permission/enablement failure as a valid empty daily report or repeatedly retries permanent misconfiguration.
detection: Classify authorization/enablement outcomes separately from successful empty data; record required and granted scope evidence without secrets.
response: Mark source unavailable and retain last valid coverage; request correct authorized credential via normal setup when implementation reaches account discovery.
test_assertion: Failed scope cannot advance complete-through watermark or generate zero activity; forecast output reports limited/unavailable coverage.
residual_limit: Public documentation does not establish the customer's endpoint entitlement.
